key_insight: The paper proves that the dimension of a simple connected GHZ graph is bounded by a function of its vertex connectivity, giving a new connectivity-based limit on how large a GHZ state can be.
engineering_relevance: This sharpens theoretical limits for photonic GHZ-state generation, helping experimental quantum optics teams estimate when a graph-based design can or cannot yield high-dimensional multipartite entanglement.
method: Derive an upper bound on GHZ graph dimension in terms of vertex connectivity: 2^(κ(G)-1) + C(κ(G), 2).
Extend the analysis to related graph measures, including edge connectivity and maximum degree.
Build on prior results that settled low-connectivity cases and strengthen the overall conjecture landscape.
evidence_signal: The result is theoretical and proof-based, using graph connectivity properties to establish new dimension bounds rather than experimental datasets.
watch_item: The bound applies to simple connected GHZ graphs and may be loose for specific instances, so practical experimental tightness still needs case-by-case validation.
